metadata.title: Comprehensive Master Instrument Catalog for Concert Band, Brass Band, and Wind Band
metadata.description: Complete reference catalog containing name, standard tuning/key, sounding transposition, clef, instrument family, ensemble distribution, and usage notes for wind, brass, string, keyboard, and percussion instruments.

ensemble_definitions.Concert Band: Also known as Symphonic Band or Wind Ensemble. Composed of full woodwind, brass, percussion sections, and double bass/piano/harp.
ensemble_definitions.Brass Band: Traditional British-style brass band with strictly defined 28-player instrumentation: cornets, flugelhorn, tenor horns, baritones, trombones, euphoniums, tubas (EEb and BBb basses), and percussion.
ensemble_definitions.Wind Band / Military Band: Large-scale symphonic or military wind formation blending full woodwinds, expanded brass (cornets, trumpets, mellophones/horns), marching basses/sousaphones, and marching/concert percussion.

instruments.name: Piccolo
instruments.sounding_transposition: Sounds 1 octave higher than written
instruments.role: Auxiliary / Standard Section Lead High Voice
instruments.notes: Ubiquitous in concert and military bands for upper-register brilliance and tutti doubling.

instruments.name: D♭ Piccolo
instruments.sounding_transposition: Sounds a minor 9th higher than written
instruments.notes: Standard in late 19th and early 20th century American and European military band arrangements (Sousa marches originally scored for D♭ piccolo).

instruments.name: Concert Flute
instruments.sounding_transposition: Concert pitch (non-transposing)
instruments.notes: Typically divided into 1st and 2nd flute parts; standard sections contain 4 to 8 players.

instruments.name: Alto Flute
instruments.sounding_transposition: Sounds a perfect 4th lower than written
instruments.notes: Frequently used in modern symphonic band repertoire for rich, velvety lyrical passages.

instruments.name: Bass Flute
instruments.sounding_transposition: Sounds 1 octave lower than written
instruments.notes: Found in contemporary large-ensemble works and dedicated flute choir features.

instruments.name: Oboe
instruments.sounding_transposition: Concert pitch (non-transposing)
instruments.notes: Usually 1st and 2nd oboe; primary tuning benchmark instrument in concert bands.

instruments.name: English Horn (Cor Anglais)
instruments.sounding_transposition: Sounds a perfect 5th lower than written
instruments.notes: Major expressive voice in masterworks (Holst, Grainger, Maslanka, Reed).

instruments.name: Oboe d'Amore
instruments.sounding_transposition: Sounds a minor 3rd lower than written
instruments.notes: Rarely scored in transcriptions (e.g. Ravel, Bach) and select contemporary band works.

instruments.name: Bassoon
instruments.sounding_transposition: Concert pitch (non-transposing)
instruments.notes: Standard instrumentation calls for Bassoon 1 and 2, reinforcing low clarinets, saxophones, and euphoniums.

instruments.name: Contrabassoon
instruments.sounding_transposition: Sounds 1 octave lower than written
instruments.notes: Provides foundation pedal reed tone down to sub-contra B♭/A.

instruments.name: Heckelphone
instruments.sounding_transposition: Sounds 1 octave lower than written
instruments.notes: Baritone oboe member, occasional appearance in avant-garde and large European wind scores.

instruments.name: A♭ Piccolo Clarinet
instruments.sounding_transposition: Sounds a minor 7th higher than written
instruments.notes: Featured in traditional Italian and Spanish civil/military bands (banda civica/militare) and clarinet choirs.

instruments.name: E♭ Sopranino Clarinet
instruments.sounding_transposition: Sounds a minor 3rd higher than written
instruments.notes: Crucial lead color in advanced concert band literature, military marches, and wind ensembles.

instruments.name: D Clarinet
instruments.sounding_transposition: Sounds a major 2nd higher than written
instruments.notes: Seen mainly in older European concert band transcriptions (Strauss, Molter); today almost universally transposed to E♭ clarinet.

instruments.name: B♭ Clarinet (Soprano)
instruments.sounding_transposition: Sounds a major 2nd lower than written
instruments.notes: The violin equivalent of the wind band. Divided into 1st, 2nd, and 3rd parts, often with 9–20 players total.

instruments.name: A Clarinet
instruments.sounding_transposition: Sounds a minor 3rd lower than written
instruments.notes: Standard in orchestras, but occasionally specified in band works (e.g. Percy Grainger, David Maslanka) or orchestral transcriptions.

instruments.name: Basset Horn
instruments.sounding_transposition: Sounds a perfect 5th lower than written
instruments.notes: Featured in classical transcriptions (Mozart, Mendelssohn) and specialist clarinet choir features.

instruments.name: E♭ Alto Clarinet
instruments.sounding_transposition: Sounds a major 6th lower than written
instruments.notes: Bridges soprano and bass clarinets; standard in American mid-century symphonic band scoring.

instruments.name: B♭ Bass Clarinet
instruments.sounding_transposition: Sounds a major 9th lower than written (French notation in treble clef)
instruments.notes: Standard section contains 1 to 3 players; critical bridge between woodwinds and brass basses.

instruments.name: EE♭ Contra-Alto Clarinet
instruments.sounding_transposition: Sounds 1 octave and a major 6th lower than written
instruments.notes: Often preferred in academic concert bands for easier response and agility compared to BB♭ contrabass.

instruments.name: BB♭ Contrabass Clarinet
instruments.sounding_transposition: Sounds 2 octaves and a major 2nd lower than written
instruments.notes: Adds profound sub-harmonic depth; capable of descending to sounding B♭0.

instruments.name: Soprillo Saxophone (Piccolo Saxophone)
instruments.sounding_transposition: Sounds 1 octave and a major 2nd higher than written
instruments.notes: Smallest pitched saxophone (sounding up to F7); rare novelty or saxophone choir feature.

instruments.name: E♭ Sopranino Saxophone
instruments.sounding_transposition: Sounds a minor 3rd higher than written
instruments.notes: Appears in European military band scores and modern saxophone ensemble repertoire.

instruments.name: B♭ Soprano Saxophone
instruments.sounding_transposition: Sounds a major 2nd lower than written
instruments.notes: Regularly called for in contemporary concert band literature (Grainger, Husa, Mackey, Ticheli).

instruments.name: E♭ Alto Saxophone
instruments.sounding_transposition: Sounds a major 6th lower than written
instruments.notes: Standard instrumentation includes 1st and 2nd Alto Saxophones; versatile melodic and harmonic voice.

instruments.name: B♭ Tenor Saxophone
instruments.sounding_transposition: Sounds a major 9th lower than written
instruments.notes: Essential middle-register voice, frequently pairing with euphoniums, French horns, and bassoons.

instruments.name: E♭ Baritone Saxophone
instruments.sounding_transposition: Sounds 1 octave and a major 6th lower than written
instruments.notes: Usually features a low A key in modern bands; provides punchy bass lines and reed foundation.

instruments.name: B♭ Bass Saxophone
instruments.sounding_transposition: Sounds 2 octaves and a major 2nd lower than written
instruments.notes: Common in early 20th century bands (Sousa, Gilmore) and revived in modern concert band scores.

instruments.name: EE♭ Contrabass Saxophone
instruments.sounding_transposition: Sounds 2 octaves and a major 6th lower than written
instruments.notes: Gigantic sub-bass saxophone; also seen in modern 'Tubax' configuration.

instruments.name: E♭ Soprano Cornet
instruments.sounding_transposition: Sounds a minor 3rd higher than written
instruments.frequency: Standard in Brass Band, Common in Wind Band
instruments.notes: Sole upper-register brass crown in traditional British brass bands (1 player); also used for high color in concert bands.

instruments.name: B♭ Cornet
instruments.sounding_transposition: Sounds a major 2nd lower than written
instruments.notes: In Brass Bands, makes up 9 players (4 Solo Cornets, 1 Repiano, 2 Second Cornets, 2 Third Cornets). In Concert Bands, historically distinct from trumpets (Cornet 1/2).

instruments.name: B♭ Repiano Cornet
instruments.sounding_transposition: Sounds a major 2nd lower than written
instruments.notes: Dedicated seat in British brass bands acting as utility soloist and bridge between soprano and lower cornets.

instruments.name: B♭ Flugelhorn
instruments.sounding_transposition: Sounds a major 2nd lower than written
instruments.frequency: Standard in Brass Band, Common in Concert Band
instruments.notes: 1 player in standard Brass Band (essential bridge to Tenor Horns); frequently used for lyrical solos in concert band works.

instruments.name: Piccolo Trumpet
instruments.sounding_transposition: Sounds a minor 7th (in B♭) or major 6th (in A) higher than written
instruments.notes: Four-valved instrument used for clarino baroque transcriptions and contemporary wind ensemble works.

instruments.name: E♭ / D Trumpet
instruments.sounding_transposition: Sounds a minor 3rd (in E♭) or major 2nd (in D) higher than written
instruments.notes: Often specified for classical transcriptions (Haydn, Hummel) and high fanfare passages.

instruments.name: B♭ Trumpet
instruments.sounding_transposition: Sounds a major 2nd lower than written
instruments.notes: Standard concert band section comprises 3 parts (often 2–3 players each). Note: Excluded from traditional British brass bands, where cornets reign.

instruments.name: C Trumpet
instruments.sounding_transposition: Concert pitch (non-transposing)
instruments.notes: Frequently utilized by professional wind ensembles and college bands playing orchestral repertoire.

instruments.name: Bass Trumpet
instruments.sounding_transposition: Sounds a major 9th lower than written (in B♭)
instruments.notes: Occasionally called for in large military bands and works by Stravinsky, Wagner, or modern wind composers.

instruments.name: E♭ Tenor Horn (Alto Horn)
instruments.sounding_transposition: Sounds a major 6th lower than written
instruments.frequency: Standard in Brass Band, Common in Military Band
instruments.notes: Standard in British brass bands (Solo, 1st, and 2nd Tenor Horn). Referred to as 'Alto Horn' in North America.

instruments.name: French Horn (Double Horn)
instruments.sounding_transposition: Sounds a perfect 5th lower than written (in F)
instruments.role: Core Harmonic Warmth & Melodic Horn Voice
instruments.notes: Standard section of 4 horns (Horns 1, 2, 3, 4). Excluded from standard British brass bands.

instruments.name: F / E♭ Mellophone
instruments.sounding_transposition: Sounds a perfect 5th lower (in F) or major 6th lower (in E♭)
instruments.frequency: Standard in Marching/Outdoor Bands, Historical in Concert Band
instruments.notes: Commonly replaces French horns in marching wind bands and outdoor military formations.

instruments.name: Wagner Tuba (Tenor / Bass)
instruments.sounding_transposition: Sounds a major 2nd lower (B♭) or perfect 5th lower (F)
instruments.notes: Played with a horn mouthpiece by French hornists; used in transcriptions (Bruckner, Wagner, Strauss) and extended modern wind works.

instruments.name: B♭ Baritone Horn
instruments.sounding_transposition: Sounds a major 9th lower than written in treble clef (or concert pitch in bass clef)
instruments.frequency: Standard in Brass Band, Common in Wind Band
instruments.notes: Standard in British brass bands (1st and 2nd Baritone). Narrower cylindrical bore than euphonium, producing a leaner, lighter tone.

instruments.name: B♭ Euphonium
instruments.sounding_transposition: Sounds a major 9th lower than written in treble clef (or concert pitch in bass clef)
instruments.clef: Bass Clef (Concert pitch in Concert Band) / Treble Clef (Transposing in Brass Band)
instruments.notes: Wide conical bore with warm cello-like timbre. 2 players in brass band (Solo Euphonium & 2nd Euphonium); 2–4 players in concert band.

instruments.name: Alto Trombone
instruments.sounding_transposition: Concert pitch in alto/treble clef, or transposing up a minor 3rd depending on edition
instruments.notes: Used in early music transcriptions, classical wind serenades, and select modern symphonic wind scores.

instruments.name: Tenor Trombone (Slide Trombone)
instruments.sounding_transposition: Concert pitch in bass clef (Concert Band); sounds major 9th lower than written in treble clef (Brass Band)
instruments.notes: In Brass Band: 1st and 2nd Tenor Trombones reading transposing treble clef. In Concert Band: 1st and 2nd Trombones reading non-transposing bass/tenor clef.

instruments.name: Bass Trombone
instruments.sounding_transposition: Concert pitch (non-transposing)
instruments.role: Core Low Brass Voice & Rhythmic Punch
instruments.notes: Equipped with 1 or 2 rotary/axial valves. Unique in British brass bands as the ONLY brass instrument reading non-transposing bass clef.

instruments.name: Contrabass Trombone
instruments.sounding_transposition: Concert pitch (non-transposing)
instruments.notes: Double-slide or valve-extended contrabass instrument used in monumental wind ensemble works.

instruments.name: Valve Trombone
instruments.sounding_transposition: Sounds a major 9th lower than written (treble) or concert pitch (bass)
instruments.frequency: Common in Southern European / Latin American Bands
instruments.notes: Widely used in Italian, Spanish, Austrian, and Latin American wind bands for rapid valve agility while marching.

instruments.name: E♭ Tuba (EE♭ Bass)
instruments.sounding_transposition: Concert pitch in bass clef (Concert Band); sounds 1 octave + major 6th lower in treble clef (Brass Band)
instruments.notes: Known as 'EE♭ Bass' in British Brass Bands (2 players). Celebrated for lyrical agility and clear upper-bass definition.

instruments.name: B♭ Tuba (BB♭ Bass)
instruments.sounding_transposition: Concert pitch in bass clef (Concert Band); sounds 2 octaves + major 2nd lower in treble clef (Brass Band)
instruments.notes: Known as 'BB♭ Bass' in British Brass Bands (2 players). Forms the monumental foundation of both brass and wind bands.

instruments.name: C Tuba (CC Tuba)
instruments.sounding_transposition: Concert pitch (non-transposing)
instruments.notes: Standard instrument for orchestral tuba players in the USA, frequently preferred in American collegiate wind ensembles.

instruments.name: F Tuba
instruments.sounding_transposition: Concert pitch (non-transposing)
instruments.notes: Used widely for solo repertoire, higher tuba parts, and lighter texture wind ensemble works.

instruments.name: Sousaphone
instruments.sounding_transposition: Concert pitch (non-transposing bass clef)
instruments.notes: Designed under John Philip Sousa's direction to cast warm bass tone upward and over the band.

instruments.name: Helicon
instruments.sounding_transposition: Concert pitch (non-transposing bass clef)
instruments.notes: Predecessor to the sousaphone, coiling around the torso; common in European cavalry and military bands.

instruments.name: String Bass (Double Bass / Contrabass)
instruments.sounding_transposition: Sounds 1 octave lower than written
instruments.notes: Standard member of the modern concert band/wind ensemble, providing pizzicato clarity and warm sustained low notes.

instruments.name: Cello (Violoncello)
instruments.sounding_transposition: Concert pitch (non-transposing)
instruments.notes: Standard in traditional Spanish wind bands (bandas de música) and Italian municipal bands; occasional guest in symphonic wind works.

instruments.name: Concert Harp
instruments.sounding_transposition: Concert pitch (non-transposing)
instruments.notes: Featured extensively in contemporary masterworks (Grainger, Persichetti, Husa, Barnes, Whitacre).

instruments.name: Electric Bass Guitar
instruments.sounding_transposition: Sounds 1 octave lower than written
instruments.notes: Often doubles or replaces the tuba/double bass in jazz, pop, Broadway, and wind rock settings.

instruments.name: Concert Grand Piano
instruments.sounding_transposition: Concert pitch (non-transposing)
instruments.notes: Vital orchestral texture in 20th and 21st-century wind band repertoire.

instruments.name: Celesta
instruments.sounding_transposition: Sounds 1 octave higher than written
instruments.notes: Steel plates struck by felt hammers, operated via keyboard; used for delicate fairy-like textures.

instruments.name: Synthesizer / Electronic Organ
instruments.sounding_transposition: Concert pitch (transposition user-defined)
instruments.notes: Used for pipe organ emulations, sub-bass 32' pedal points, and atmospheric sound design.

instruments.name: Timpani (Kettledrums)
instruments.key: Tuned to pitch (typically set of 4 or 5 drums: 32", 29", 26", 23", 20")
instruments.sounding_transposition: Concert pitch (non-transposing)
instruments.role: Core Harmonic Bass Rhythms & Dynamic Climax
instruments.notes: Crucial anchor in both brass bands and concert bands. Pitch range typically covers D2 to A3.

instruments.name: Glockenspiel (Orchestra Bells)
instruments.sounding_transposition: Sounds 2 octaves higher than written
instruments.notes: Penetrating high metallic bell tone, often doubling upper woodwinds or soprano brass.

instruments.name: Xylophone
instruments.sounding_transposition: Sounds 1 octave higher than written
instruments.notes: Bright, sharp acoustic attack; essential in both modern concert band and brass band percussion sections.

instruments.name: Marimba
instruments.key: C (Tuned rosewood/padauk bars, usually 4.3 or 5.0 octaves)
instruments.sounding_transposition: Concert pitch (non-transposing)
instruments.role: Warm Resonant Chords & Rapid Keyboard Runs
instruments.notes: Deep, warm, resonant acoustic timbre; foundational voice in modern percussion writing.

instruments.name: Vibraphone
instruments.sounding_transposition: Concert pitch (non-transposing)
instruments.role: Lyrical Sustained Chords & Motor Vibrato Effects
instruments.notes: Equipped with motorized rotating butterflies in resonator tubes and a damper pedal.

instruments.name: Tubular Bells (Chimes)
instruments.key: C (Tuned brass tubes, usually C4 to F5 / G5)
instruments.sounding_transposition: Concert pitch (non-transposing)
instruments.notes: Simulates real church bells; prominent in climaxes and ceremonial marches.

instruments.name: Crotales (Antique Cymbals)
instruments.sounding_transposition: Sounds 2 octaves higher than written
instruments.role: Pristine High Shimmer & Bowed Metallic Textures
instruments.notes: Can be struck with hard mallets or bowed with a double bass bow for eerie, shimmering harmonics.

instruments.name: Snare Drum
instruments.sounding_transposition: Indefinite pitch
instruments.notes: Foundational instrument in all band types; metal/gut snares provide crisp articulation.

instruments.name: Concert Bass Drum (Gran Cassa)
instruments.sounding_transposition: Indefinite pitch
instruments.notes: Large suspended calfskin or plastic head drum providing foundational dynamic weight.

instruments.name: Clash Cymbals (Crash Cymbals / Hand Cymbals)
instruments.sounding_transposition: Indefinite pitch
instruments.notes: Hand-held paired bronze cymbals (typically 18" to 22" Viennese or French crash).

instruments.name: Suspended Cymbal
instruments.sounding_transposition: Indefinite pitch
instruments.notes: Played with yarn/felt mallets, drumsticks, or scraped with a triangle beater/coin.

instruments.name: Tam-Tam (Gong)
instruments.sounding_transposition: Indefinite pitch
instruments.notes: Unpitched, flat-faced hammered bronze disc; provides colossal dramatic crashes and quiet omens.

instruments.name: Triangle
instruments.sounding_transposition: Indefinite pitch
instruments.notes: Steel bar bent into an open triangle; cuts clearly through full fortissimo tutti.

instruments.name: Tambourine
instruments.sounding_transposition: Indefinite pitch
instruments.notes: Wood shell with calfskin head and metal jingles; executed with thumb rolls, shakes, and knee-fist strikes.
